# dsh-memory
**Persistent, human-editable memory for DeepSeek Harness.**
English | 中文

The agent forgets everything when a session ends. `dsh-memory` gives it one small place to
remember
— a plain JSONL file you can read, edit, delete, and back up.
Tell it once:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Open a brand-new session tomorrow:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

No tool call, no re-explanation, no "as you mentioned earlier" — the fact is simply in the
prompt fr

-explanation, no "as you mentioned earlier" — the fact is simply in the
prompt from the first token.
## Why this instead of `AGENTS.md`?

`AGENTS.md` is project guidance: static, shared, committed to the repository, written by
whoever mai

ntains it. Memory is personal: written by the agent as it learns you, kept outside
the repo, and app
lied to every project.
| | `AGENTS.md` | `dsh-memory` |

| Written by | a human, by hand | the agent, during work |
| Scope | one repository | you, everywher

e |
| Lives in | the repo (committed) | `~/.dsh/memory/` (private) |
| Grows | when someone edits it

| automatically, deduplicated |
| Budget | whatever fits | capped in bytes, newest first |
They compose. Keep coding conventions in `AGENTS.md`, keep *you* in memory.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then restart DSH. That is the whole setup: there is nothing to configure, no API key, no
network acc
ess, no background service.
Install from a local checkout
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or add it by hand to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Use
Nothing to learn: memory is used by talking.
| You say | What happens |

| "I always use pnpm." | Saved as a durable preference |
| "以后的提交信息都用中文" | Saved |
| "Our staging DB

is read-only, never write to it." | Saved — a constraint worth not re-learning |
| "What do I usual

ly prefer?" | The agent searches memory |
| "Forget what I said about pnpm." | List, find, forget |

The agent decides when something is worth remembering; the tool's description tells it to
skip trans
ient task state and anything already readable from a file.
## How it works
Two mechanisms, one store:

1. **The `memory` tool** — one tool with four actions (`save`, `search`, `list`, `forget`).
`save` f

olds whitespace and de-duplicates case-insensitively, so restating a fact updates
it instead of pili

ng up near-copies.
2. **A prompt section** — registered through `ctx.systemPrompt.section()` at orde

r `10150`,
after the Web surface and before the persona suffix. Its text is a *function*, so it is
r

e-rendered at every assembly: a fact saved in one session is visible in the next step of
every other
one, with no restart.

The section is byte-bounded (`maxBytes`, default 4096). Newest entries win; the section says
how man

y older ones were left out, and a tight budget degrades to a shorter header rather
than silently dro

left out, and a tight budget degrades to a shorter header rather
than silently dropping the feature.
## Storage
[代码示例省略，未执行]
One JSON object per line:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **Yours.** It is a text file: `cat`, `grep`, `git`, edit it by hand, delete a line.
- **Safe to ed

it.** A malformed line is skipped, not fatal — one typo does not disable the plugin.
- **Atomic.** W

rites go to a temp file and are renamed, so a crash mid-write cannot truncate it.
- **Local.** Nothi
ng is uploaded. There is no account, no telemetry, no network code at all.
## Configuration
Optional; the defaults are what most people want. In your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `dir` | `<DSH home>/memory` | Store directory. `DSH_HOME` is honoured when set. |
| `maxBytes` | `

4096` | Byte budget for the injected section. |
| `maxEntries` | `500` | Hard cap on stored entries;
the oldest is evicted first. |
## Limits
Honest list of what this version does **not** do:

- **One global store.** Memories apply to every workspace. Per-project scope is not implemented.
- *

*Substring search.** No embeddings, no ranking — `search` is a case-insensitive substring
match on c

ontent and tags. That is enough for a few hundred short facts and costs nothing.
- **No automatic ex

traction.** The agent saves explicitly; there is no post-turn summariser
burning tokens behind your

back.
- **No UI.** No settings page, no panel — a tool and a prompt section only.
- **Prompt tokens.

** The section costs what it costs: 4 KB is roughly 1 K tokens on every
request. Lower `maxBytes` if
that matters to you.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.x` — the Host API this plugin targets is the one shipped in `0.2.2-rc.1`
(`c

tx.tools.register`, `ctx.systemPrompt.section`)
- Node `>= 20`
- No dependencies. The plugin imports
only Node's standard library.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`smoke` drives the tool and the prompt section against a temporary store: de-duplication,
budget tri

mming, eviction, malformed-line resilience, argument validation, and unload
cleanup. No test framewo
rk, no install step.

`cordis` mounts the plugin through the real `@deepseek-ai/cordis` and proves the two things
a stub c

annot: that `ctx.plugin()` loads it, and that unloading removes both registrations.
It skips when th

e runtime is not installed, which is why CI runs only the first — run it
inside a DSH installation.
